subject: Question re: zero inflated negative binomial model for count data

messages.author: 448410b8993f8a6a
messages.subject: Question re: zero inflated negative binomial model for count data
parts:
Hi all, I am attempting to run zero-inflated negative binomial model for count data within 6 treatment groups, but one of the groups has absolutely no variance (all data points are zero), and when I try to run the model I get the following error: 

Call: zeroinfl(formula = Max.Sept ~ Treatment, data = np_d, 
         dist = "negbin", EM = TRUE)

Error in solve.default(as.matrix(fit$hessian)) : 
  Lapack routine dgesv: system is exactly singular: U[10,10] = 0

I have searched the help forums, but not found any clear answers other than to simplify my model (I only have one independent variable, can't simplify it much more).
I am thinking that perhaps the lack of variance in one of the treatment groups causes the test to fail because it cannot estimate the parameter, but that is only my guess. I could artificially add some variance (like inject some 1's into the misbehaving treatment group, but then I reduce the number of zeros, and this seems a bit hokey anyway). 

Does anyone have any suggestions? Thank you!!
